      What the robot does

      The same thing you would do with ten minutes and a burner wallet.

      1 · OPENS IT

      The coin's own site

      The site comes from the coin's listing, never from whoever asks. It loads in a real Chromium browser and the screen is recorded from the first frame.

      2 · USES IT

      Clicks like a buyer

      It finds the main button, connects a wallet, fills the form and goes for the core action: launch, swap, create, play. Up to 12 steps.

      3 · STAMPS IT

      WORKS or NOTHING WORKS

      Dead buttons, "coming soon" and pages that only link to pump.fun get the red stamp. A product that reaches a real transaction gets the green one.

      Don't trust the robot. Check it.

      The stamp is an opinion. Everything under it is measured.

      Every test is a public run

      Tests run on GitHub Actions in the open. Each result links to its run log: every step, every click, the verdict. Read the code ↗

      The recording is the proof

      The full session is saved to IPFS and shown with the verdict. If the stamp is wrong, the video shows it.

      Evidence overrules the AI

      WORKS needs at least one click that measurably did something. NOTHING WORKS cannot stand next to a real transaction for an on-chain program. The counters decide, not the wording on the page.

      The wallet can't lose anything

      A fresh key per test, with nothing in it. It connects and signs messages. Every transaction is recorded and declined.

      Questions

      My coin got NOTHING WORKS and the product is real.

      Watch the recording first: it shows exactly where the robot got stuck. Fix what a new visitor can't get past, then anyone holding 1,000,000 $PROVEN can re-test right away, and everyone can after 24 hours. Old verdicts stay visible with their date.

      What counts as WORKS?

      The robot used the core thing the site says it does, or got as far as a real transaction or signature request. Live data that answers to its input counts. A dashboard screenshot does not.

      Can a site talk the robot into a green stamp?

      Page text is treated as untrusted, and the measured evidence overrules the model: a page where no click does anything cannot be stamped WORKS, whatever it says.

      Which coins can be tested?

      Any Solana coin that lists its own website. Coins with only an X or Telegram link have no product to open, so there is nothing to test.

      Is a green stamp a reason to buy?

      No. It means the product did something when a robot used it today. It says nothing about the team, the chart or tomorrow.
